{{Short description|Theorem in differential geometry}}
In the mathematical field of [[differential geometry]], the existence of [[isothermal coordinates]] for a ([[pseudo-Riemannian manifold|pseudo-]])[[Riemannian metric]] is often of interest. In the case of a metric on a two-dimensional space, the existence of isothermal coordinates is unconditional. For higher-dimensional spaces, the '''Weyl–Schouten theorem''' (named after [[Hermann Weyl]] and [[Jan Arnoldus Schouten]]) characterizes the existence of isothermal coordinates by certain equations to be satisfied by the [[Riemann curvature tensor]] of the metric.

Existence of isothermal coordinates is also called [[conformally flat|conformal flatness]], although some authors refer to it instead as ''local conformal flatness''; for those authors, conformal flatness refers to a more restrictive condition.

==Theorem==
In terms of the [[Riemann curvature tensor]], the [[Ricci tensor]], and the [[scalar curvature]], the [[Weyl tensor]] of a pseudo-Riemannian metric {{mvar|g}} of dimension {{mvar|n}} is given by{{sfnm|1a1=Aubin|1y=1998|1loc=Definition 4.23}}
:<math>W_{ijkl}=R_{ijkl}-\frac{R_{ik}g_{jl}-R_{il}g_{jk}+R_{jl}g_{ik}-R_{jk}g_{il}}{n-2}+\frac{R}{(n-1)(n-2)}(g_{jl}g_{ik}-g_{jk}g_{ik}).</math>
The [[Schouten tensor]] is defined via the Ricci and scalar curvatures by{{sfnm|1a1=Aubin|1y=1998|1loc=Definition 4.23}}
:<math>S_{ij}=\frac{2}{n-2}R_{ij}-\frac{Rg_{ij}}{(n-2)(n-1)}.</math>
As can be calculated by the [[Bianchi identities]], these satisfy the relation that{{sfnm|1a1=Aubin|1y=1998|1p=118|2a1=Eisenhart|2y=1926|2p=91}}
:<math>\nabla^jW_{ijkl}=\frac{n-3}{2}(\nabla_kS_{il}-\nabla_lS_{ik}).</math>
The '''Weyl–Schouten theorem''' says that for any pseudo-Riemannian manifold of dimension {{mvar|n}}:{{sfnm|1a1=Aubin|1y=1998|1loc=Theorem 4.24|2a1=Eisenhart|2y=1926|2loc=Section 28}}
* If {{math|''n'' ≥ 4}} then the manifold is conformally flat if and only if its Weyl tensor is zero.
* If {{math|''n'' {{=}} 3}} then the manifold is conformally flat if and only if its Schouten tensor is a [[Codazzi tensor]].
As known prior to the work of Weyl and Schouten, in the case {{math|''n'' {{=}} 2}}, every manifold is conformally flat. In all cases, the theorem and its proof are entirely local, so the topology of the manifold is irrelevant.

There are varying conventions for the meaning of conformal flatness; the meaning as taken here is sometimes instead called ''local conformal flatness''.

==Sketch of proof==
The ''only if'' direction is a direct computation based on how the Weyl and Schouten tensors are modified by a conformal change of metric. The ''if direction'' requires more work.

Consider the following equation for a 1-form {{math|''&omega;''}}:
:<math>\nabla_i\omega_j=\frac{1}{2}\omega_i\omega_j-\frac{1}{4}g^{pq}\omega_p\omega_qg_{ij}-S_{ij}</math>
Let {{math|''F''<sup>''&omega;'',''g''</sup>}} denote the tensor on the right-hand side. The [[Frobenius theorem (differential topology)|Frobenius theorem]]<ref>For the direct version being used, see {{harvnb|Abraham|Marsden|Ratiu|1988|loc=Example 6.4.25D}}; {{harvnb|Lee|2013|loc=Proposition 19.29}}; {{harvnb|Warner|1983|loc=Remarks 1.61}}.</ref> states that the above equation is locally solvable if and only if
:<math>\partial_k\Gamma_{ij}^p\omega_p+\Gamma_{ij}^pF_{kp}^{\omega,g}+\frac{1}{2}F_{ki}^{\omega,g}\omega_j+\frac{1}{2}\omega_iF_{kj}^{\omega,g}-\frac{1}{4}\partial_kg^{pq}\omega_p\omega_qg_{ij}-\frac{1}{2}g^{pq}\omega_pF_{kq}^{\omega,g}g_{ij}-\frac{1}{4}g^{pq}\omega_p\omega_q\partial_kg_{ij}-\partial_kS_{ij}</math>
is symmetric in {{mvar|i}} and {{mvar|k}} for any 1-form {{math|''&omega;''}}. A direct cancellation of terms<ref>This uses the identity <math>W_{kijp}=R_{kijp}-\frac{1}{2}g_{ip}S_{jk}+\frac{1}{2}g_{ij}S_{kp}+\frac{1}{2}g_{kp}S_{ij}-\frac{1}{2}g_{jk}S_{ip}.</math></ref> shows that this is the case if and only if
:<math>{W_{kij}}^p\omega_p=\nabla_kS_{ij}-\nabla_iS_{jk}</math>
for any 1-form {{math|''&omega;''}}. If {{math|''n'' {{=}} 3}} then the left-hand side is zero since the Weyl tensor of any three-dimensional metric is zero; the right-hand side is zero whenever the Schouten tensor is a Codazzi tensor. If {{math|''n'' ≥ 4}} then the left-hand side is zero whenever the Weyl tensor is zero; the right-hand side is also then zero due to the identity given above which relates the Weyl tensor to the Schouten tensor.

As such, under the given curvature and dimension conditions, there always exists a locally defined 1-form {{math|''&omega;''}} solving the given equation. From the symmetry of the right-hand side, it follows that {{math|''&omega;''}} must be a [[Closed and exact differential forms|closed form]]. The [[Poincaré lemma]] then implies that there is a real-valued function {{mvar|u}} with {{math|''&omega;'' {{=}} ''du''}}. Due to the formula for the [[Ricci curvature]] under a conformal change of metric, the (locally defined) pseudo-Riemannian metric {{math|e<sup>''u''</sup>''g''}} is Ricci-flat. If {{math|''n'' {{=}} 3}} then every Ricci-flat metric is flat, and if {{math|''n'' ≥ 4}} then every Ricci-flat and Weyl-flat metric is flat.{{sfnm|1a1=Aubin|1y=1998|1loc=Theorem 4.24|2a1=Eisenhart|2y=1926|2loc=Section 28}}
